chunks: When the witnesses testify against the adulterer that he sat with her in the position of a man with his wife, the hadd (prescribed punishment) shall be enacted upon him.
He (the Imam) said: And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: O Allah, if You were to give me power over al-Mughira, I would certainly stone him.

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: hadd — the fixed, divinely-prescribed punishment for certain crimes including zina
key_terms.الْمُغِيرَة: al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba — a figure accused of adultery during the caliphate of Umar, whose punishment was averted when one witness recanted
key_terms.مَجْلِسَ الرَّجُلِ مِنِ امْرَأَتِهِ: the position/sitting of a man with his wife — a legal euphemism for the sexual position establishing penetration

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia jurisprudential standard for establishing the hadd punishment for adultery according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) states that testimony of witnesses that the accused took the intimate position with a woman suffices to establish the hadd punishment for zina (unlawful sexual intercourse). The Imam then recalls that Imam Ali (AS) repeatedly invoked Allah against al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba — a companion of the caliph Umar who had been accused of adultery but escaped the hadd on a legal technicality — expressing that had he the authority, he would have carried out the stoning. This hadith reflects both Shia jurisprudential standards for establishing the hadd and the historical tension over justice not being served in a politically sensitive case during the early caliphate period.
